One table per namespace, in the order of the guide: the call, which leads to its page in the [reference](/reference/), and what it does. Optional parameters end with `?`. Types and options are detailed in the reference.

## Essentials

### nc.config

See [the guide](/start/configuration/) and [the namespace in the reference](/reference/config/).

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`nc.config.set(settings)`](/reference/config/set/) | Changes the language and the time zone used by `num` and `time`. |
| [`nc.config.get()`](/reference/config/get/) | The settings now in use. |

### nc.logger

See [the guide](/essentials/logger/) and [the namespace in the reference](/reference/logger/).

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`nc.logger.log(...args)`](/reference/logger/log/) | Prints a message without a badge. |
| [`nc.logger.trace(...args)`](/reference/logger/trace/) | Very detailed diagnostics, shown only at the `trace` level. |
| [`nc.logger.debug(...args)`](/reference/logger/debug/) | Diagnostics for developers, shown at the `debug` level (the default when `DEBUG` is set). |
| [`nc.logger.info(...args)`](/reference/logger/info/) | An informational message. |
| [`nc.logger.success(...args)`](/reference/logger/success/) | A success message. |
| [`nc.logger.warn(...args)`](/reference/logger/warn/) | A warning, written to stderr. |
| [`nc.logger.error(...args)`](/reference/logger/error/) | An error, written to stderr. |
| [`nc.logger.fatal(...args)`](/reference/logger/fatal/) | A fatal error, written to stderr. |
| [`nc.logger.group(label?)`](/reference/logger/group/) | Prints a label and indents what follows, until `groupEnd()`. |
| [`nc.logger.groupEnd()`](/reference/logger/group-end/) | Closes the current group. |
| [`nc.logger.timeStart(label?)`](/reference/logger/time-start/) | Starts a named timer. |
| [`nc.logger.timeEnd(label?)`](/reference/logger/time-end/) | Prints the time since `timeStart()` with the same label. |
| [`nc.logger.table(rows, options?)`](/reference/logger/table/) | Prints rows as a table. |
| [`nc.logger.box(text, options?)`](/reference/logger/box/) | Prints text in a box. |
| [`nc.logger.divider(title?)`](/reference/logger/divider/) | Prints a horizontal line, with an optional title in it. |
| [`nc.logger.setLevel(level)`](/reference/logger/set-level/) | Sets the minimum level. |
| [`nc.logger.getLevel()`](/reference/logger/get-level/) | The current minimum level. |
| [`nc.logger.isLevelEnabled(level)`](/reference/logger/is-level-enabled/) | Would this level be printed? |
| [`nc.logger.configure(options)`](/reference/logger/configure/) | Changes several settings at once. |
| [`nc.logger.create(options?)`](/reference/logger/create/) | Creates a logger with its own settings. |

### nc.fs

See [the guide](/essentials/fs/) and [the namespace in the reference](/reference/fs/).

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`nc.fs.read(path, encoding)`](/reference/fs/read/) | Reads a file as text, or as a Buffer with `"buffer"`. |
| [`nc.fs.readJSON(path, fallback?, options?)`](/reference/fs/read-json/) | Reads a JSON file. |
| [`nc.fs.readLines(path)`](/reference/fs/read-lines/) | Reads a text file as lines. |
| [`nc.fs.write(path, data, options?)`](/reference/fs/write/) | Writes a file atomically, creating its folders. |
| [`nc.fs.writeJSON(path, data, options?)`](/reference/fs/write-json/) | Writes a value as JSON, atomically, creating folders. |
| [`nc.fs.append(path, data)`](/reference/fs/append/) | Appends to a file, creating it and its folders if needed. |
| [`nc.fs.exists(path)`](/reference/fs/exists/) | Does a file or folder exist at this path? |
| [`nc.fs.isFile(path)`](/reference/fs/is-file/) | Is it an existing file? |
| [`nc.fs.isFolder(path)`](/reference/fs/is-folder/) | Is it an existing folder? |
| [`nc.fs.stat(path)`](/reference/fs/stat/) | Size, dates and type of a path. |
| [`nc.fs.size(path)`](/reference/fs/size/) | The size of a file in bytes, or the total size of every file in a folder (nested ones included, links not followed). |
| [`nc.fs.hash(path, options?)`](/reference/fs/hash/) | Hashes a file in chunks, so huge files are fine. |
| [`nc.fs.list(folder?, options?)`](/reference/fs/list/) | The files, the folders, or both, inside a folder. |
| [`nc.fs.glob(pattern, options?)`](/reference/fs/glob/) | Finds paths matching a glob pattern: `*` (anything but `/`), `**` (any depth), `?`, `[abc]` and `{js,ts}`. |
| [`nc.fs.find(name, options?)`](/reference/fs/find/) | Searches a folder tree for the first file or folder with this name, closest first. |
| [`nc.fs.findUp(name, options?)`](/reference/fs/find-up/) | Looks for a file or folder in a folder, then in its parent, and so on up to the root. |
| [`nc.fs.ensureFile(path)`](/reference/fs/ensure-file/) | Makes sure a file exists (an empty one if needed) and returns its absolute path. |
| [`nc.fs.ensureFolder(path)`](/reference/fs/ensure-folder/) | Makes sure a folder exists, its parents too, and returns its absolute path. |
| [`nc.fs.touch(path)`](/reference/fs/touch/) | Updates a file's modification time, creating the file if needed, like the Unix `touch` command. |
| [`nc.fs.copy(source, dest, options?)`](/reference/fs/copy/) | Copies a file or a whole folder, like `cp -r`. |
| [`nc.fs.move(source, dest, options?)`](/reference/fs/move/) | Moves or renames a file or folder, across drives too. |
| [`nc.fs.remove(path, options?)`](/reference/fs/remove/) | Deletes a file or a folder, whichever it is. |
| [`nc.fs.resolve(path?)`](/reference/fs/resolve/) | The absolute version of a path, whether it exists or not, resolved the way every function of `nc.fs` does it: `./` and `../` start from the file that calls it, anything else relative starts from the working directory, and an absolute path stays as it is. |
| [`nc.fs.temp(prefix?)`](/reference/fs/temp/) | Creates a new, unique folder in the system's temp directory. |
| [`nc.fs.sanitizeFilename(name, options?)`](/reference/fs/sanitize-filename/) | Turns any text into a file name that works on Windows, macOS and Linux: forbidden characters are replaced, invisible and text direction characters are removed, reserved names like `CON`, `NUL .txt` or `COM¹` are prefixed, and the length is capped. |
| [`nc.fs.watch(path, options?)`](/reference/fs/watch/) | Watches a file or folder for changes. |

### nc.env

See [the guide](/essentials/env/) and [the namespace in the reference](/reference/env/).

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`nc.env.parse(content, options?)`](/reference/env/parse/) | Parses the text of a `.env` file: quotes, multi-line values, `export`, comments, escapes, and `${VAR}` expansion (except in single quotes). |
| [`nc.env.load(files?, options?)`](/reference/env/load/) | Loads `.env` files into `process.env`. |
| [`nc.env.get(name, fallback?)`](/reference/env/get/) | Reads a variable, with a fallback. |
| [`nc.env.has(name)`](/reference/env/has/) | Is the variable set, even to an empty string? |
| [`nc.env.required(name)`](/reference/env/required/) | Reads a variable that must be set and not empty. |
| [`nc.env.string(name, options?)`](/reference/env/string/) | Reads a string. |
| [`nc.env.number(name, options?)`](/reference/env/number/) | Reads a number. |
| [`nc.env.boolean(name, options?)`](/reference/env/boolean/) | Reads a boolean: `true`/`false`, `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no` or `on`/`off`. |
| [`nc.env.port(name, options?)`](/reference/env/port/) | Reads a port number. |
| [`nc.env.url(name, options?)`](/reference/env/url/) | Reads an absolute URL. |
| [`nc.env.duration(name, options?)`](/reference/env/duration/) | Reads a duration like `"30s"` or `"1h30m"` and returns milliseconds. |
| [`nc.env.list(name, options?)`](/reference/env/list/) | Reads a comma-separated list. |
| [`nc.env.json(name, options?)`](/reference/env/json/) | Reads a JSON value. |
| [`nc.env.oneOf(name, values, options?)`](/reference/env/one-of/) | Reads a variable that must be one of the given values. |
| [`nc.env.validate(spec, options?)`](/reference/env/validate/) | Checks all your variables at once and returns a typed, frozen config. |
| [`nc.env.example(spec)`](/reference/env/example/) | Writes the `.env.example` that goes with a `validate()` spec: one entry per variable, with its description, type and default. |
| [`nc.env.mode()`](/reference/env/mode/) | `NODE_ENV`, or `"development"` when it's not set. |
| [`nc.env.isProduction()`](/reference/env/is-production/) | Is `NODE_ENV` set to `"production"`? |
| [`nc.env.isDevelopment()`](/reference/env/is-development/) | Is `NODE_ENV` `"development"`, or not set? |
| [`nc.env.isTest()`](/reference/env/is-test/) | Are we running tests? |

### nc.assert

See [the guide](/essentials/is/) and [the namespace in the reference](/reference/assert/).

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`nc.assert(condition, message?)`](/reference/assert/assert/) | Throws an `AssertionError` if `condition` is falsy. |
| [`nc.assert.type(value, guard, message?)`](/reference/assert/type/) | Throws an `AssertionError` unless `value` passes `guard`. |

### nc.errors

See [the guide](/basics/errors/) and [the namespace in the reference](/reference/errors/).

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`nc.errors.NodeComfortError`](/reference/errors/node-comfort-error/) | Base class of every node-comfort error. |
| [`nc.errors.AssertionError`](/reference/errors/assertion-error/) | Thrown by `nc.assert()` and `nc.assert.type()`. |
| [`nc.errors.TimeoutError`](/reference/errors/timeout-error/) | Thrown when something takes too long: `func.timeout`, `async.poll`, HTTP requests, `emitter.waitFor`... |
| [`nc.errors.AbortError`](/reference/errors/abort-error/) | Thrown when an operation is cancelled with an `AbortSignal`. |
| [`nc.errors.ValidationError`](/reference/errors/validation-error/) | Thrown when data doesn't match a schema or when environment variables are invalid. |
| [`nc.errors.HttpError`](/reference/errors/http-error/) | Thrown by `nc.http` when the response status isn't 2xx (unless you pass `throwHttpErrors: false`), and for network failures (`status` 0). |
| [`nc.errors.JWTError`](/reference/errors/jwt-error/) | Thrown by `nc.crypto.verifyJWT()`. |
| [`nc.errors.ProcessError`](/reference/errors/process-error/) | Thrown by `nc.sys.run()` and `nc.sys.exec()` when a command fails, is killed or times out. |
| [`nc.errors.SQLiteError`](/reference/errors/sqlite-error/) | Thrown by `nc.sqlite.SQLite` when a statement fails. |
| [`nc.errors.CircuitOpenError`](/reference/errors/circuit-open-error/) | Thrown by `execute()` of a circuit from `nc.circuit.create()` while the circuit is open: the call was rejected without running. |

## Data

### nc.str

See [the guide](/data/str/) and [the namespace in the reference](/reference/str/).

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`nc.str.capitalize(input)`](/reference/str/capitalize/) | Uppercases the first character and lowercases the rest. |
| [`nc.str.upperFirst(input)`](/reference/str/upper-first/) | Uppercases the first character and leaves the rest alone. |
| [`nc.str.lowerFirst(input)`](/reference/str/lower-first/) | Lowercases the first character and leaves the rest alone. |
| [`nc.str.humanize(input)`](/reference/str/humanize/) | Turns an identifier into a label people can read. |
| [`nc.str.titleCase(input)`](/reference/str/title-case/) | Uppercases the first letter of each word and leaves the rest alone. |
| [`nc.str.sentenceCase(input)`](/reference/str/sentence-case/) | Lowercases everything, then capitalizes the start of each sentence. |
| [`nc.str.camelCase(input)`](/reference/str/camel-case/) | Converts to `camelCase`. |
| [`nc.str.pascalCase(input)`](/reference/str/pascal-case/) | Converts to `PascalCase`. |
| [`nc.str.snakeCase(input)`](/reference/str/snake-case/) | Converts to `snake_case`. |
| [`nc.str.kebabCase(input)`](/reference/str/kebab-case/) | Converts to `kebab-case`. |
| [`nc.str.constantCase(input)`](/reference/str/constant-case/) | Converts to `CONSTANT_CASE`. |
| [`nc.str.dotCase(input)`](/reference/str/dot-case/) | Converts to `dot.case`. |
| [`nc.str.words(input)`](/reference/str/words/) | Splits text into words. |
| [`nc.str.deburr(input)`](/reference/str/deburr/) | Removes accents (`é` becomes `e`) and spells out special Latin letters (`ß` becomes `ss`, `æ` becomes `ae`). |
| [`nc.str.slugify(input, options?)`](/reference/str/slugify/) | Turns text into a URL slug: no accents, lowercase, words joined by dashes. |
| [`nc.str.squish(input)`](/reference/str/squish/) | Collapses runs of whitespace into single spaces and trims the ends. |
| [`nc.str.stripTags(input)`](/reference/str/strip-tags/) | Removes HTML tags and keeps the text. |
| [`nc.str.escapeHTML(input)`](/reference/str/escape-html/) | Escapes `& < > " '` so the text is safe inside HTML content and quoted attribute values. |
| [`nc.str.unescapeHTML(input)`](/reference/str/unescape-html/) | Decodes HTML entities: named ones like `&amp;` and `&nbsp;`, and numeric ones like `&#233;`. |
| [`nc.str.escapeRegExp(input)`](/reference/str/escape-reg-exp/) | Escapes regex special characters so the text matches literally. |
| [`nc.str.length(input)`](/reference/str/length/) | Counts visible characters. |
| [`nc.str.byteLength(input, encoding?)`](/reference/str/byte-length/) | Size of the text in bytes once encoded, UTF-8 by default. |
| [`nc.str.count(input, search)`](/reference/str/count/) | Counts how many times `search` appears, without overlaps. |
| [`nc.str.truncate(input, length, options?)`](/reference/str/truncate/) | Shortens text to `length` visible characters, ending with `…` when cut. |
| [`nc.str.chunk(input, size)`](/reference/str/chunk/) | Splits text into pieces of `size` visible characters. |
| [`nc.str.between(input, start, end)`](/reference/str/between/) | Returns the text between `start` and the next `end`, or `undefined` if a marker is missing. |
| [`nc.str.splitOnce(input, separator)`](/reference/str/split-once/) | Splits at the first occurrence of `separator` only. |
| [`nc.str.lines(input)`](/reference/str/lines/) | Splits text into lines, whatever the line endings. |
| [`nc.str.padStart(input, length, char?)`](/reference/str/pad-start/) | Pads the start until the text is `length` characters long. |
| [`nc.str.padEnd(input, length, char?)`](/reference/str/pad-end/) | Pads the end until the text is `length` characters long. |
| [`nc.str.center(input, length, char?)`](/reference/str/center/) | Centers text within `length` characters. |
| [`nc.str.indent(input, prefix?)`](/reference/str/indent/) | Indents every non-empty line. |
| [`nc.str.dedent(input, ...values)`](/reference/str/dedent/) | Removes the indentation shared by all lines, and blank first and last lines. |
| [`nc.str.wrap(input, options?)`](/reference/str/wrap/) | Wraps text so no line is longer than `width` visible characters. |
| [`nc.str.reverse(input)`](/reference/str/reverse/) | Reverses text without breaking emoji or accents. |
| [`nc.str.mask(input, options?)`](/reference/str/mask/) | Hides part of a string, like a card number or a token. |
| [`nc.str.initials(input, max?)`](/reference/str/initials/) | The initials of a name, in uppercase. |
| [`nc.str.plural(value, forms, options?)`](/reference/str/plural/) | Picks the right plural for a count, following the rules of the language, and puts the formatted count in front. |
| [`nc.str.template(input, data, options?)`](/reference/str/template/) | Fills `{placeholders}` with values. |
| [`nc.str.ensurePrefix(input, prefix)`](/reference/str/ensure-prefix/) | Adds `prefix` unless the text already starts with it. |
| [`nc.str.ensureSuffix(input, suffix)`](/reference/str/ensure-suffix/) | Adds `suffix` unless the text already ends with it. |
| [`nc.str.removePrefix(input, prefix)`](/reference/str/remove-prefix/) | Removes `prefix` if the text starts with it. |

| [`nc.str.random(size?, options?)`](/reference/str/random/) | A random string. |

| [`nc.arr.sumBy(array, iteratee?)`](/reference/arr/sum-by/) | Adds up a number from each item. |
| [`nc.arr.averageBy(array, iteratee?)`](/reference/arr/average-by/) | The average of a number from each item, or `0` for an empty array. |
| [`nc.arr.maxBy(array, iteratee?)`](/reference/arr/max-by/) | The item with the highest value. |

## Functions and async

### nc.func

See [the guide](/flow/func/) and [the namespace in the reference](/reference/func/).

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`nc.func.debounce(fn, wait, options?)`](/reference/func/debounce/) | Waits for a pause of `wait` ms between calls, then runs once with the latest arguments. |
| [`nc.func.throttle(fn, interval, options?)`](/reference/func/throttle/) | Runs at most once every `interval` ms, however often it's called. |
| [`nc.func.once(fn)`](/reference/func/once/) | Runs `fn` the first time only; later calls return the same result. |
| [`nc.func.memoize(fn, options?)`](/reference/func/memoize/) | Caches results by arguments. |
| [`nc.func.delay(fn, ms, ...args)`](/reference/func/delay/) | Waits `ms`, then calls `fn` with the arguments and resolves with its result. |
| [`nc.func.attempt(fn)`](/reference/func/attempt/) | Wraps a function so it resolves to `[error, value]` instead of throwing. |
| [`nc.func.promisify(fn)`](/reference/func/promisify/) | Turns a callback-style function into one that returns a promise. |
| [`nc.func.batch(fn, options?)`](/reference/func/batch/) | Turns many single calls into few grouped ones. |
| [`nc.func.dedupe(fn, keyOf?)`](/reference/func/dedupe/) | Makes concurrent calls with the same arguments share one run. |
| [`nc.func.pipe(f1)`](/reference/func/pipe/) | Chains functions from left to right: `pipe(f, g)(x)` is `g(f(x))`. |
| [`nc.func.pipeAsync(f1, f2)`](/reference/func/pipe-async/) | Like `pipe()`, for functions that may be async: each one is awaited before the next runs. |
| [`nc.func.compose(f2, f1)`](/reference/func/compose/) | Chains functions from right to left: `compose(f, g)(x)` is `f(g(x))`. |
| [`nc.func.curry(fn, arity?)`](/reference/func/curry/) | Lets you pass a function's arguments a few at a time. |
| [`nc.func.partial(fn, ...preset)`](/reference/func/partial/) | Fixes the first arguments of a function. |
| [`nc.func.negate(predicate)`](/reference/func/negate/) | The opposite of a predicate. |
| [`nc.func.after(n, fn)`](/reference/func/after/) | Does nothing for the first `n - 1` calls, then calls `fn` every time. |
| [`nc.func.before(n, fn)`](/reference/func/before/) | Calls `fn` for the first `n - 1` calls, then keeps returning the last result. |
| [`nc.func.noop(..._args)`](/reference/func/noop/) | Does nothing. |
| [`nc.func.identity(value)`](/reference/func/identity/) | Returns its argument. |

### nc.async

See [the guide](/flow/async/) and [the namespace in the reference](/reference/async/).

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`nc.async.sleep(duration, options?)`](/reference/async/sleep/) | Resolves after a delay, given in milliseconds or as a duration string. |
| [`nc.async.map(items, fn, options?)`](/reference/async/map/) | Maps items through an async function, with at most `concurrency` calls at once. |
| [`nc.async.forEach(items, fn, options?)`](/reference/async/for-each/) | Runs an async function for every item, with a concurrency limit. |
| [`nc.async.filter(items, predicate, options?)`](/reference/async/filter/) | Keeps the items that pass an async test, with a concurrency limit. |
| [`nc.async.series(tasks, options?)`](/reference/async/series/) | Runs async functions one after the other and returns their results. |
| [`nc.async.parallel(tasks, options?)`](/reference/async/parallel/) | Runs async functions at the same time, or a few at once with `concurrency`, and returns their results in order. |
| [`nc.async.limit(concurrency)`](/reference/async/limit/) | A limiter: wrap calls with it, and at most `concurrency` run at once while the rest wait their turn. |
| [`nc.async.rateLimit(max, interval)`](/reference/async/rate-limit/) | A rate limiter: at most `max` calls start within any `interval`. |
| [`nc.async.queue(options?)`](/reference/async/queue/) | A task queue with a concurrency limit, priorities, pause and per-task timeouts. |
| [`nc.async.mutex()`](/reference/async/mutex/) | A mutex: tasks given to `run()` never overlap. |
| [`nc.async.deferred()`](/reference/async/deferred/) | A promise along with its `resolve` and `reject`. |
| [`nc.async.settle(promises)`](/reference/async/settle/) | Waits for every promise and sorts successes from failures. |
| [`nc.async.props(object)`](/reference/async/props/) | Like `Promise.all`, for an object of promises. |
| [`nc.async.poll(fn, options?)`](/reference/async/poll/) | Calls `fn` until it returns something truthy, and resolves with it. |
| [`nc.async.abortable(promise, signal?)`](/reference/async/abortable/) | Makes any promise give up when a signal fires. |
| [`nc.async.retry(fn, options?)`](/reference/async/retry/) | Calls `fn` until it succeeds, waiting between attempts. |
| [`nc.async.timeout(promise, ms, message?)`](/reference/async/timeout/) | Rejects with a `TimeoutError` if the promise takes longer than `ms`. |
| [`nc.async.to(promise)`](/reference/async/to/) | Awaits a promise and gives you `[error, value]` instead of throwing, so you don't need a try/catch. |
| [`nc.async.when(predicate, payload?, options?)`](/reference/async/when/) | Checks a condition at a regular interval and tells you when it's true. |

| [`cache.keys()`](/reference/cache/keys/) | Fresh keys, least recently used first. |
| [`cache.values()`](/reference/cache/values/) | Fresh values, least recently used first. |
| [`cache.entries()`](/reference/cache/entries/) | Fresh `[key, value]` pairs, least recently used first. |

### nc.crypto

See [the guide](/system/crypto/) and [the namespace in the reference](/reference/crypto/).

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`nc.crypto.hash(data, options?)`](/reference/crypto/hash/) | Hashes data, SHA-256 in hex by default. |
| [`nc.crypto.hmac(data, secret, options?)`](/reference/crypto/hmac/) | An HMAC signature: a hash keyed with a secret. |
| [`nc.crypto.verifyHmac(data, signature, secret, options?)`](/reference/crypto/verify-hmac/) | Checks an HMAC signature you received, in constant time. |
| [`nc.crypto.safeEqual(a, b)`](/reference/crypto/safe-equal/) | Compares two secrets in constant time, so the comparison can't leak anything through timing, not even their lengths. |

| [`nc.crypto.verifyPassword(password, stored)`](/reference/crypto/verify-password/) | Checks a password against a stored hash, in constant time: scrypt hashes from `hashPassword()`, and Argon2 PHC strings (`$argon2id$`, `$argon2i$`, `$argon2d$`) from here or from another library. |
| [`nc.crypto.needsRehash(stored, options?)`](/reference/crypto/needs-rehash/) | Was this hash made with another algorithm, or with weaker settings than yours (lower cost, a key under 32 bytes, a salt under 16)? |

| [`nc.crypto.encrypt(data, secret, options?)`](/reference/crypto/encrypt/) | Encrypts data with AES-256-GCM, which also detects tampering. |
| [`nc.crypto.decrypt(payload, secret, options)`](/reference/crypto/decrypt/) | Decrypts what `encrypt()` produced. |
| [`nc.crypto.signJWT(payload, secret, options?)`](/reference/crypto/sign-jwt/) | Creates a signed JSON Web Token. |
| [`nc.crypto.decodeJWT(token)`](/reference/crypto/decode-jwt/) | Reads a JWT without checking it. |
| [`nc.crypto.verifyJWT(token, secret, options?)`](/reference/crypto/verify-jwt/) | Verifies a JWT: algorithm, signature, expiry, and whichever claims you require. |
| [`nc.crypto.generateKeyPair(algorithm?, options?)`](/reference/crypto/generate-key-pair/) | Makes a pair of keys for signing JWTs: the private one signs, the public one verifies. |
| [`nc.crypto.totpSecret(bytes?)`](/reference/crypto/totp-secret/) | A new two-factor secret, in the Base32 format authenticator apps expect. |
| [`nc.crypto.totp(secret, options?)`](/reference/crypto/totp/) | The current 6-digit code for a two-factor secret, as shown by authenticator apps. |
| [`nc.crypto.verifyTOTP(token, secret, options?)`](/reference/crypto/verify-totp/) | Checks a code typed by a user. |
| [`nc.crypto.totpStep(code, secret, options?)`](/reference/crypto/totp-step/) | Finds which time step a code typed by a user belongs to. |
| [`nc.crypto.totpURI(secret, options)`](/reference/crypto/totp-uri/) | The `otpauth://` link to show as a QR code when a user turns on 2FA. |
| [`nc.crypto.randomBytes(size)`](/reference/crypto/random-bytes/) | Secure random bytes. |
| [`nc.crypto.randomInt(min, max)`](/reference/crypto/random-int/) | A secure random integer from `min` to `max`, both included, with no bias. |
| [`nc.crypto.toBase64(data, options?)`](/reference/crypto/to-base64/) | Encodes to Base64, or URL-safe Base64. |
| [`nc.crypto.fromBase64(text, options)`](/reference/crypto/from-base64/) | Decodes Base64 or URL-safe Base64. |

| [`db.isOpen`](/reference/sqlite/is-open/) | Whether the connection is open. |
| [`db.native`](/reference/sqlite/native/) | The underlying `node:sqlite` database, for anything not covered here. |
